result.topic: Validating TLS certs against internal-CA-signed PAN-OS/Panorama management interfaces from a Python `requests`-based client, without verify=False — how PAN's own OSS tools handle it, and what to change in this prototype.

confirmedFacts.claim: requests' own `verify` parameter natively accepts a path (string) to a CA_BUNDLE file or a hashed cert directory, instead of only True/False. It also auto-reads REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE (falling back to CURL_CA_BUNDLE) env vars when set.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "You can pass verify the path to a CA_BUNDLE file or directory with certificates of trusted CAs... This list of trusted CAs can also be specified through the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable. If REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is not set, CURL_CA_BUNDLE will be used as fallback."

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's PanXapi class exposes an `ssl_context` constructor kwarg. If the caller does NOT supply one, pan.xapi silently disables server certificate verification entirely (uses ssl._create_unverified_context()) because PAN-OS devices commonly ship self-signed certs. Verification only happens if the caller builds and passes their own ssl.SSLContext.
confirmedFacts.evidence: if self.ssl_context is None: kwargs['context'] = ssl._create_unverified_context() else: kwargs['context'] = self.ssl_context  (docstring: "Because many PAN-OS systems use a self-signed certificate, pan.xapi will disable the default server certificate verification... ssl_context can be used to enable verification.")

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's own CLI wrapper (panxapi.py) demonstrates the concrete pattern for supplying an internal/enterprise CA bundle: it exposes --cafile/--capath flags, builds an ssl.SSLContext with CERT_REQUIRED + check_hostname=True, calls context.load_verify_locations(cafile=cafile, capath=capath), then passes that context into PanXapi(ssl_context=...).
confirmedFacts.evidence: def create_ssl_context(cafile, capath): context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_SSLv23); context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED; context.check_hostname = True; context.load_verify_locations(cafile=cafile, capath=capath)

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-os-python (the successor SDK, used by pan-os-ansible) wraps pan.xapi.PanXapi via an internal XapiWrapper, but its PanDevice.generate_xapi() hardcodes the kwargs it forwards (api_key, hostname, port, timeout, pan_device only) — it never accepts or forwards an ssl_context, verify, or CA-bundle parameter. PanDevice.__init__ itself has no such parameter either.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def generate_xapi(self): kwargs = {"api_key": self.api_key, "hostname": self.hostname, "port": self.port, "timeout": self.timeout, "pan_device": self}; return PanDevice.XapiWrapper(**kwargs)

confirmedFacts.claim: This is a known, unresolved limitation: a pan-os-python maintainer confirmed the library 'does not check certificates by default,' and the thread contains no supported way to point it at a custom CA bundle -- only environment-level workarounds (PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0, disabling urllib3 warnings), none of which add verification against a custom CA.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Maintainer Brian Torres-Gil: "pandevice does not check certificates by default, so you should not get this error by default."

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-os-ansible's module_utils provider arg-spec (which builds a pan-os-python PanDevice under the hood) exposes only ip_address/username/password/api_key/port/serial_number for connections -- there is no validate_certs, ca_cert, or ssl_context parameter anywhere in the collection's connection layer.
confirmedFacts.evidence: provider arg spec options: ip_address (required), username (default admin), password, api_key, port (default 443), serial_number -- no cert/verify-related key present

confirmedFacts.claim: terraform-provider-panos (current Go-rewrite, v2.x, generated via pan-os-codegen on top of the pango SDK) exposes only a boolean `skip_verify_certificate` (env var PANOS_SKIP_VERIFY_CERTIFICATE) in its provider schema. There is no ca_certificate / CA-bundle-path provider argument.
confirmedFacts.evidence: `skip_verify_certificate` (Boolean) (For https protocol) Skip verifying the HTTPS certificate. Environment variable: `PANOS_SKIP_VERIFY_CERTIFICATE`.

confirmedFacts.claim: The underlying pango Go SDK's Client struct only has a `SkipVerifyCertificate bool` field, which maps to `tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: c.SkipVerifyCertificate}` -- there is no RootCAs/x509.CertPool/CACert field. The only way to inject a custom trust store in pango is to construct and assign your own *http.Transport (with your own tls.Config{RootCAs: pool}) to Client.Transport before calling Setup(), entirely bypassing the SkipVerifyCertificate flag -- this is Go-specific and has no Python/requests analog in this SDK.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Note that the SkipVerifyCertificate setting is only used if you do not specify a HTTP transport yourself." -- if c.Transport == nil { c.Transport = &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: c.SkipVerifyCertificate}} }

confirmedFacts.claim: Palo Alto's own official repo for management-cert diagnostics (mgmt-cert-check) itself calls `requests.post(url, verify=False, ...)` throughout and calls `requests.packages.urllib3.disable_warnings()`. It is NOT a usable template for validating against a custom CA -- its purpose is inspecting/reporting on the cert itself (a diagnostic tool), and it deliberately never verifies.

Official PAN-OS docs recommend replacing the management interface's self-signed cert with one issued by an enterprise/internal CA specifically so client systems already trust it via their existing trust store; if a self-signed cert is kept instead, the doc says to deploy that self-signed root CA cert to all client systems. It does not give Python/requests-specific or API-automation-specific guidance.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "You can simplify your Certificate Deployment by using a certificate that the client systems already trust."

confirmedFacts.claim: The SSL/TLS Service Profile doc frames trust from the opposite direction (client must already have the CA in its trust list) and gives no guidance on exporting the chain specifically for API/automation consumers.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "In the client systems that request firewall services, the certificate trust list (CTL) must include the certificate authority (CA) certificate that issued the certificate specified in the SSL/TLS service profile."

confirmedFacts.claim: The only official, generic (not automation-specific) mechanism for getting a usable CA/cert file off a PAN-OS device is the GUI/API certificate export: Device > Certificate Management > Certificates > Export, choosing PEM format; or programmatically via the XML API type=export&category=certificate (params: certificate-name, format=pem|pkcs12|pkcs10, include-key, passphrase). Neither the GUI export doc nor the Export Files (API) doc mentions using the export for client-side trust-store/API-client configuration -- that's an inferred, not documented, use.
confirmedFacts.evidence: type=export, category=certificate, certificate-name=<name>, format=<pkcs12|pem|pkcs10>, include-key=<yes|no>; documented use cases are user/device authentication and SSL decryption, not client trust-store configuration

remainingGaps: No official Palo Alto documentation or SDK explicitly documents the requests-library `verify=<CA-bundle-path>` pattern for PAN-OS API clients -- this report's recommendation is an inference from requests' own official docs applied to the existing prototype's requests-based architecture, not something confirmed inside a PAN-authored source.

None of the four named OSS projects actually use Python's `requests` library as their core PAN-OS transport (pan-python/pan-os-python/pan-os-ansible use urllib + ssl.SSLContext; terraform-provider-panos/pango use Go net/http) -- so there is no directly-transferable requests-based code snippet from an established PAN-OS integration; the pattern had to be translated from pan-python's ssl_context/load_verify_locations approach and requests' own verify=path semantics.

Whether the Suncoast management interfaces are already running an enterprise-CA-issued cert (vs. self-signed) is unknown -- cannot confirm without live-device access, so it's unconfirmed whether main.py's config even needs a CA-bundle path yet or whether the mgmt cert must first be replaced per Palo Alto's own recommended flow.

No live-device test of `requests.get(..., verify='/path/to/internal-ca.pem')` against an actual PAN-OS/Panorama management HTTPS endpoint was possible (no test device) -- the recommendation rests on requests' documented, general-purpose behavior, not a PAN-OS-specific confirmation that the mgmt web server presents a chain requests can validate cleanly (e.g., whether it sends intermediate certs, which affects whether the caller needs the leaf-issuing intermediate or just the root in the bundle).

community.paloaltonetworks.com (now live.paloaltonetworks.com) searches surfaced only tangential threads (cert expiration checks, cert-chain-for-VPN questions); no LIVEcommunity thread was found giving a maintainer-endorsed requests+CA-bundle pattern specifically for PAN-OS API automation.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: No functional/logic change needed in _get_with_retry / _xml_request -- requests already treats verify=<str path> and verify=<bool> correctly when passed through as-is (confirmed: requests.readthedocs.io advanced usage). Only update the type hint and docstring: change `verify_tls: bool = True` in PanBaseConnector.__init__ to `verify_tls: Union[bool, str] = True` (import Union from typing) and note in the docstring that a string value is treated as a path to a CA bundle file, or a directory of hashed certs (per OpenSSL c_rehash), consistent with requests' own documented verify semantics.

Same type-hint/docstring update: `verify_tls: Union[bool, str] = True` on PanAuthClient.__init__ and PanAuthClient._verify_tls, matching pan_base.py. The requests.post(..., verify=self._verify_tls, ...) call in _generate_key needs no other change.

Update `_connector_for`'s `verify_tls: bool` type hint to `Union[bool, str]`. Document in the devices-config JSON schema (wherever fw_cfg/panorama_cfg fields are described) that `verify_tls` may be `true`, `false`, or a string filesystem path to the enterprise CA's PEM bundle -- e.g. `"verify_tls": "/etc/suncoast/pan-internal-ca.pem"` -- exported from the firewall/Panorama per docs.paloaltonetworks.com's Export a Certificate flow (Device > Certificate Management > Certificates > Export, PEM format) or supplied by Suncoast's internal PKI team directly. `fw_cfg.get("verify_tls", True)` and `panorama_cfg.get("verify_tls", True)` need no code change since JSON already round-trips strings transparently -- only the surrounding docs/comments and type hints need updating to stop implying bool-only.

As a zero-code alternative/fallback, document that operators can instead set the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable (e.g. `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/suncoast/pan-internal-ca.pem`) and leave verify_tls=true; requests will consult it automatically for every call in this prototype without any per-host config. This is lower-precedence than an explicit string path passed as verify_tls and should be called out as such if both are ever set.
